entries.canonical_text: writes from a transaction that subsequently aborts are never visible to any other transaction at any timestamp
commit timestamps are assigned monotonically: every committed transaction's ts strictly exceeds the ts of every previously committed transaction
a transaction's read snapshot is fixed at its begin timestamp; subsequent commits do not become visible to it
a row version with begin_ts and end_ts is visible to a transaction reading in the rv_begin..rv_end interval iff their visibility intervals overlap per the three-interval predicate
concurrent writes to the same row by two in-flight transactions cause one of them to abort with a write-write conflict
at most one write transaction is active at any time
Writers and VACUUM serialize: at most one of them can modify the database at any instant
the in-memory log header is published only after the on-disk header pwrite has completed durably
the in-memory log offset advances only after the corresponding frame pwrite has completed durably
the pending running-CRC slot is cleared by the storage abort path after an abandoned deferred-offset write
the shadow offset tracking the log's durable boundary equals the durable offset at every quiescent boundary after a truncate
the running CRC of the log is reseeded only after the truncate operation has completed durably
A sqlite_schema row version produced by logical-log recovery always carries a decodable (type, rootpage) record before it can reach checkpoint identity decoding
Replaying a committed logical log never aborts as corruption; a delete of a sqlite_schema rowid absent from the merged state is the legal no-op of a same-transaction create-then-drop
Every transaction id referenced by a live connection or open cursor remains present in the MVCC transaction map until that reference is released
Pinning and unpinning a page preserve evictable-count coherence; the counter dimension is independent of the pin dimension

entries.canonical_text: The materialized evictable counter never exceeds the number of resident pages, so the spill room estimate can never claim more reclaimable pages than the cache holds
The cache's materialized evictable-page counter stays equal to the true number of evictable resident pages after every cache operation
A coherent evictable counter equals the true evictable count if and only if no counted page is pinned, multiply-owned, or locked

backed_by.turso: s202_evictable_count_equality_regime — evictable_count == count_evictable_pages() in the unobstructed regime conformance gate (page-cache-conformance)

entries.canonical_text: The maintained evictable counter equals the true evictable count exactly when no counted page is pinned, multiply-owned, or locked
The maintained evictable-page counter is always a conservative upper bound on the true number of strictly-evictable pages
Capacity-pressure eviction removes only fully-evictable pages, so it never evicts a dirty-unspilled page (data loss), the database header page, or a locked page
The pin-guarded removers (delete, truncate, WAL-frame cleanup) never remove a pinned page; clear is the one exception and drops pages with no pin check

backed_by.turso: s204_explicit_removal_pin_safety — truncate keeps a pinned page + clear drops even pinned (documented) conformance gate (page-cache-conformance)

entries.canonical_text: The page cache actually caches: a page is retrievable after insertion, a resident page that is not evicted or deleted is not silently lost, get and contains agree, and residency never exceeds capacity

backed_by.turso: s210_functional_contract — insert->get round-trip + capacity conformance gate (page-cache-conformance)

entries.canonical_text: The spill fast path may decline to spill only when its optimistic room estimate is trustworthy, so it never skips a spill that is genuinely required
Capacity-pressure eviction never removes a page that is currently pinned, so any page in active use stays resident as long as it is held
Growing the page cache's capacity is lossless: every resident page stays resident, the length is unchanged, and the capacity is updated to the new larger value

backed_by.turso: s211_resize_grow_preserves_residency — resize to larger capacity retains all pages conformance gate (page-cache-conformance)

entries.canonical_text: a compaction operation preserves logical content, preserves all schema and engine metadata, does not increase physical footprint, and is atomic under crash
VACUUM is atomic under crash: recovery yields either the pre-VACUUM state or the post-VACUUM state, never an intermediate
The database header's change_counter is monotonically non-decreasing across all modifying operations, including VACUUM
After VACUUM, the database file's page count equals the formal model's prediction (pre-vacuum allocated pages minus the pre-vacuum freelist)
VACUUM preserves the database's logical content
A checkpoint failure must not leak frames into the main database file
When per-commit durability is requested, a commit frame must reach stable storage via fsync before the transaction is reported as durable
find_frame never reads outside the live frame range [nbackfills, max_frame]
The WAL initialized flag is set true only after a successful sync of the wal-header
The nbackfills counter advances after frames are durable, so recovery never replays already-checkpointed frames
the WAL subsystem maintains LSN monotonicity, frame commitment ordering, recovery idempotency, checkpoint safety, and group-commit atomicity
WAL truncate is atomic: no committed frame can be observed lost across the truncate operation
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
